  • The file is generated; edit the function where it is defined and add it again. Its header records a checksum, so the builder regenerates a file nobody edited, in this session or a later one. A file that was edited by hand (or that no builder wrote), or that holds functions this builder does not have (another writer added them), is refused, so they are not lost without a word: wf.add_operation(f, overwrite=True) or wf.write(overwrite=True) replaces it. WorkflowBuilder.load reads a hand-edited file's functions and keeps the file as it is until its functions change; a file holding other top-level statements (a constant, a class) is then refused with their names, since a generated file holds imports and functions only.
  • A workflow that already names another operation funcs file takes no add_operation: add the functions to that file.

docs.title: Running again, and changing a step
docs.text:
Run the script, or the notebook from the top, as often as you like. A file is rewritten only when its content changes, and wf.run() runs only the steps that have not run or are stale. Its first line names the steps it runs and those it keeps, and each kept step gets a line of its own:

[workflow] running 1 of 2 steps: chain; keeping a-alone
[workflow] step a-alone: done and current, not run again

When every step is done and current it says so and runs nothing. To run every step again, current or not, use wf.run(force=True) (on the command line, leave out --stale-only); wf.run(from_step='<id>') runs one step and every step after it.

A step is stale when something it ran with has changed: its obs_data, its params_for_id, its model's parameters file, its settings, or the workflow's functions file (any function in it, whether or not the step uses it), or when a step it takes values from is stale or ran again. wf.status() shows which.

  • To change a step, change what you pass and add it again with the same id. A dict is copied when it is added, so editing the dict afterwards changes nothing until wf.add_calibration('chain', obs_data=edited, ...) is called again. The step keeps its place.
  • wf.run(force=True) runs every step again. wf.run(from_step='chain') runs that step and those after it, and wf.run(only='chain') just that step; both reuse the earlier results, which must be current.
  • wf.run(ranks=4) runs mpiexec -n 4 on the written file.
  • wf.remove_step(id) takes a step out. WorkflowBuilder.load(path_or_directory) makes a builder from an existing workflow file.

What the builder writes, in wf.directory, when wf.write() is called (run, plan, status, model and plot_step call it first):

calibration_workflow.json          the workflow; its paths are relative to this directory
data/<step>_obs_data.json          an obs_data given as a dict
data/<step>_params_for_id.json     a params_for_id given as entries
<name>_operation_funcs.py          the functions given to add_operation, with their imports
.workflow_builder_files.json       which of these files a builder wrote, for wf.clean()
workflow_output/<name>/            the run (wf.output_dir), see Outputs below

Two steps given the same dict share one file, named after the first. Keep files of your own out of data/.

Removing or renaming a step leaves its data files behind. wf.clean() lists the files the builder wrote for this workflow that no workflow in the directory names any more, and wf.clean(delete=True) moves them to data/removed/; it deletes nothing. A file is only ever listed when a builder wrote it, its content is still what was written, and no JSON file at the top of the directory names it. Nothing under workflow_output/ is touched.

After a run, wf.result(id) is what the step recorded (a calibration's values and best_cost, a reduction's chosen parameters, each kind's files as paths), wf.step_dir(id) its output directory, wf.plot_step(id) plots a calibration's fit (as png; formats=('png', 'pdf') for more), and wf.model(id) (or wf.model('target')) generates the model with the values found so far, under the run's models/<id>/. Every path the builder returns (wf.directory, wf.path, wf.output_dir, wf.write(), wf.step_dir(id), the files in wf.result(id)) is a pathlib.Path.

A step's options are dicts under the names the schema gives them: sa_options, ia_options, emulator_settings, and for a reduction wf.add_reduction(id, sensitivity_from=..., param_reduction_options={'method': 'pca', ...}).

docs.title: From the command line
docs.text:
The written file is an ordinary workflow: CUFLynx opens it, pack_workflow carries its data and functions file, and the command runs it. The command's default output directory is workflow_output/<name> beside the workflow file, which is the builder's wf.output_dir, so the command continues the same run from any directory:

cuflynx-calibration-workflow wf_python/calibration_workflow.json --stale-only

--stale-only runs what wf.run() would; without it the command runs every step, and --only and --from-step are as in Python.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "workflow_name": "aorta_then_circulation",
  "module_library_dirs": ["../module_library"],
  "settings": {"param_id_method": "CMA-ES", "dt": 0.001,
               "optimiser_options": {"num_calls_to_function": 400}},
  "target": "resources/circulation_module_array.csv",
  "steps": [
    {"id": "aorta-compliance",
     "model": "resources/aorta_only_module_array.csv",
     "obs_data": "data/aorta_obs_data.json",
     "params_for_id": "data/aorta_params_for_id.json"},
    {"id": "whole-circulation",
     "model": "resources/circulation_module_array.csv",
     "obs_data": "data/circulation_obs_data.json",
     "params_for_id": "data/circulation_params_for_id.json",
     "fixed_from": ["aorta-compliance"]}
  ]
}

Paths are relative to the workflow file. A model is one of:

  • a module array of CA, as "resources/<prefix>_module_array.csv" (or .json). Its parameters file is <prefix>_parameters.json beside it, or name it: {"module_array": "...", "parameters": "..."}.
  • a module of a module library, as {"module_type": "i_M", "version": "Argus2026_v01", "parameterisation": "davis2020_wistar"}. The library is found through module_library_dirs (see module parameterisations).
  • (a step's, with a module-array target) a selection of the target's instances, as {"select": ["C"]} or {"select": ["heart/lv"]} (see Calibrating a selection).
  • an external Python model, as {"external_model_path": "heat1d_model.py"}. It is never generated, so it is the target and every step's model, and its parameters keep their component/variable names. See Calibration workflows in the external solvers guide.
  • a CellML model, as {"cellml_model_path": "model.cellml"}, or {"cellml_model_path": "model.cellml", "parameters": "values.json"} with a parameters file ({"<component>": {"<variable>": {"value": ..., "units": ...}}}) whose values replace the CellML's. Its parameters are its constants, named component/variable (states and computed variables are not), and every component is a vessel. A params_for_id, set entry or sweep may also name a constant as a calibration of the same file reads it (global/q_lv_init for parameters_global/q_lv_init, aortic_root/C for parameters/C_aortic_root): the step resolves the name to the constant, and its results, the merged target and the calibrated files name the constant. It is never generated: a step runs a flattened copy, <step_id>/model/generated_models/<step_id>/<step_id>.cellml, with the step's values written in, and <step_id>_parameters.json beside it lists every constant's value. As for an external model, it is the target and every step's model. It runs as model_type: cellml (default solver CVODE_myokit), or, with model_type python, casadi_python or aadc_python in the settings (the workflow's or a step's, with solver and solver_info as for any model), as the Python generated from that copy, <step_id>.py beside it; the values still go into the CellML. cpp and external_python are refused. write_calibrated writes <stem>_calibrated_parameters.json and <stem>_calibrated.cellml beside it, and a pack copies it with the files it imports, at their paths relative to it.

Your own CellML as the target, fitted and then its uncertainty quantified at the fit, from Python (the files are tests/data/workflow_parity/'s; the paths are relative to the working directory):

from libcuflynx.calibration_workflow import WorkflowBuilder, cellml_model

wf = WorkflowBuilder('lv', target=cellml_model('lotka_volterra.cellml'), directory='lv_workflow',
                     settings={'solver': 'CVODE_myokit', 'dt': 0.01,
                               'param_id_method': 'CMA-ES',
                               'optimiser_options': {'num_calls_to_function': 300}})
wf.add_calibration('fit', obs_data='lv_obs_data.json', params_for_id='lv_params_for_id.json')
wf.add_uq('posterior', obs_data='lv_obs_data.json', params_for_id='lv_params_for_id.json',
          uq_options={'num_steps': 200}, result_from='fit')
wf.run(write_calibrated=True)       # also lotka_volterra_calibrated.cellml beside the source
print(wf.result('fit')['best_fit'], wf.result('posterior')['distribution_dir'])
Key Meaning target the model the results are merged into module_library_dirs module libraries, relative to the file (more with --module-library-dir); needed when a model is a library module settings user_inputs settings for every step: param_id_method, optimiser_options, solver, solver_info, dt, pre_time, sim_time, UQ_options, DEBUG, ... (the model, obs_data, params_for_id and output paths are the workflow's, and cannot be set) step id a label for the step, unique in the file: other steps refer to it, and it names the step's output directory. It is not a module or parameter name. step model, obs_data, params_for_id what the step calibrates, and against what step module_map a module array whose modules are named differently in the target: {"aorta": "aortic_root"} step submodule / module where a library module sits in the target: a submodule of a library supermodule target (i_M, or soma/i_M when nested), or a module of a module-array target; inferred when the module occurs once step fixed_from steps whose calibrated values -- and the values they were themselves given -- are fixed in this step's model, except those it calibrates itself. An entry {"step": "fit_a", "parameters": ["p_A"]} fixes only those of the step's own calibrated or set values (model names in that step), and none it was given step priors_from steps whose stored posterior becomes this step's prior (below) step store_distribution sample the posterior by MCMC after the fit and store it step start_from (calibration) a calibration or set step whose values of this step's own parameters are where its fit starts (below) step emulator_dir (calibration, sensitivity, identifiability, uq) an emulator trained outside the workflow, which the step runs on (below) step settings merged over the workflow's (one level deep, so optimiser_options add up)

A step runs after every step it takes something from (fixed_from, priors_from and the keys in Step kinds), since it needs their results; steps that pass nothing between them run in file order. Here whole-circulation runs after aorta-compliance, with the aorta's calibrated values fixed.

docs.title: Calibrating a selection
docs.text:
A step can calibrate some instances of a module-array target as they are in it, without a model file of its own:

{"id": "c-alone", "model": {"select": ["C"]},
 "obs_data": "data/c_obs.json", "params_for_id": "data/c_params.json"}

A selection runs as one of the other models:

  • one instance -- a record, or heart/lv inside a super instance -- is its library module, the record's version and parameterisation (a submodule's: its version's default), placed at that instance as "module" would place it. A selected supermodule instance is generated with the model's values for it;
  • several records are the module array they form, cut from the target. A link to a record outside the selection is dropped, which leaves that port open.

The step starts from the target's values for its instances: the entries of the target's parameters file under them, a nested instance's under its path (heart/lv; see A model's supermodule instances). Values fixed from earlier steps go over those. Its obs_data and params_for_id name vessels as the target does (C/z, heart__lv/E). For one instance, whose model is generated as mod, renamed copies are written to <step_id>/inputs/ and run from there.

A port the selection leaves open turns its boundary condition into a parameter. Give it a protocol in the step's obs_data, which sets its value while the step runs:

"protocol_info": {"pre_times": [0.0], "sim_times": [[1.0]],
                  "params_to_change": {"C/x": [[8.0]]}}

Without one, it takes the parameterisation's value or the target's row. A parameter with none of these stops the step with an UnsetParametersError, whose names list them as the target's parameters file does (C/x), so a front end can ask for their protocols. The results merge into the target like any step's: in <prefix>_calibrated_parameters.json (write_calibrated), the target's parameters file completed with every other value its model uses (its generated <prefix>_parameters.json), only the values the step calibrated change, a value inside a super instance under its path (heart/lv/E). write_calibrated_parameters_to(source, output_dir, path) writes the same file to path, and nothing else: neither the target's files nor the supermodule version's template change. It builds on the run's own _target/ generated parameters file, so a library default changed after the run does not reach the result; only a run without a target model has the target generated again, against the library as it is then. A run whose target model has a generated parameters CSV (an older libcuflynx wrote one) is refused: run the workflow again.

docs.title: Step kinds
docs.text:
A step's kind is calibration unless it says otherwise. sensitivity, emulation and identifiability run the analyses cuflynx-sensitivity, cuflynx-train-emulator and cuflynx-identifiability run, on the step's model, obs_data and params_for_id. Only the values of calibrations, set steps and combine steps are merged into the target.

A step can run on a surrogate in place of the model: on an emulator, named by the step's emulator_from or emulator_dir (below), or on a reduced-order model, which is the step's model (an external Python model).

kind What it does Needs Takes from calibration a param_id run; MCMC with store_distribution fixed_from, priors_from, start_from, emulator_from, params_for_id_from sensitivity Sobol or local sensitivity analysis sa_options in its settings fixed_from, emulator_from, result_from reduction keeps the parameters a Sobol step found most influential, or those chosen by hand ("method": "manual") sensitivity_from, param_reduction_options in its settings; no model or files (chosen by hand: params_for_id, and no sensitivity_from) emulation trains an emulator of the observables emulator_settings (optional) fixed_from, params_for_id_from identifiability Identifiability analysis (Laplace or a profile likelihood) at a step's values, or at the model's own ia_options fixed_from, result_from uq MCMC or a Laplace approximation at a step's values, or at the model's own, with no fit of its own; stores the distribution UQ_options with method mcmc (default) or laplace fixed_from, result_from, emulator_from set declares values or scales by hand, each with a reason; with "point": true they are only a point for other steps and never reach the target set; no model or files the calibration or set steps it scales combine gives one value per parameter from several steps: the values of the calibration with the lowest cost (best_fit), or each parameter's mean (mean). Its values are used in place of theirs, in later steps and in the target (below) combine_from, combine; no model or files the calibration, set or combine steps it combines sweep runs a model across chosen parameter values and keeps every run model (or "on_target": true), sweep, dt, and sim_time or an obs_data; no params_for_id fixed_from, result_from simulate runs a model once through its protocol; a sweep of no parameters model (or "on_target": true), dt, and sim_time or an obs_data; simulate.outputs or prediction items fixed_from, result_from figure calls a Python function that draws figures from other steps' results function, inputs; no model or files of data the steps its inputs name

The keys that pass something on, each naming one step of the kind shown:

Key Names a What this step gets fixed_from calibration, set or combine its values, fixed in this step's model (above) priors_from calibration with store_distribution, or uq its posterior, as a prior (below) result_from calibration, set or combine its values, including those of the parameters this step analyses: a local sensitivity, identifiability analysis or uq step is then at that point. Without it, they are at the model's own values start_from calibration, set or combine its values of the parameters this calibration fits, as the point the fit starts from combine_from calibration, set or combine (two or more) a combine step's inputs: the values it gives one of per parameter emulator_from emulation its emulator, which this step (a calibration or sensitivity) runs on instead of the model. The step names the same model, obs_data and params_for_id as the emulation step (an emulator answers only for what it was trained on) and has no fixed_from or result_from: it runs on a copy of that step's model, with the values that step was given. One exception: a calibration may take a reduction's parameters (params_for_id_from) on the emulator of the params_for_id they were reduced from. It calibrates the parameters the reduction kept and holds the emulator's other parameters at their values in the emulation step's model, so the emulator is always evaluated at every parameter it was trained on and no second emulator is trained. Its result lists the held parameters and their values under held, and the run directory has held_entries.json. A held value must be inside its params_for_id bounds. Such a step has no store_distribution or priors_from sensitivity_from sensitivity (Sobol) a reduction's indices emulator_dir (a path, not a step) an emulator trained outside the workflow, as emulator_from gives one: a directory holding emulator_metadata.json (cuflynx-train-emulator's, or an emulation step's of another run), relative to the workflow file. Not with emulator_from. Its files are hashed into the step's inputs, so a retrained emulator makes the step stale, and a pack copies it to inputs/<step_id>/. It must have been trained on the step's model, obs_data and params_for_id. The step's result_from point is only where the emulator is evaluated: it is not written into the step's model, which stays the one the emulator was trained on params_for_id_from reduction the params_for_id the reduction wrote, in place of the step's own (a calibration or emulation of the same model as the sensitivity step, or of a model with the parameters chosen by hand; a step on that emulator names the same reduction)

A calibration with start_from starts its fit at the values that step calibrated or set for its own parameters: its model is generated with them, so they are the optimiser's initial point (CMA-ES and the gradient methods start there; the genetic algorithm draws its first population at random). They are not fixed, and only the values the step fits reach the target. step_result.json records them under start_from.

{"id": "sliders", "kind": "set", "set": [
  {"parameter": "Lotka_Volterra_module/alpha", "value": 4.2, "reason": "slider position"}]},
{"id": "fit", "model": {"cellml_model_path": "lotka_volterra.cellml"},
 "obs_data": "lv_obs_data.json", "params_for_id": "lv_params_for_id.json",
 "start_from": "sliders"}

A uq step quantifies the uncertainty of its parameters at one point, without fitting: result_from a calibration's fit or a set step's values, else the model's own. Its UQ_options.method is mcmc (the walkers start in a ball about the point, as after a fit) or laplace (a Gaussian there, its covariance from the Hessian of the cost, with the step's ia_options choosing the gradient). Either way the distribution is stored in <step_id>/distribution/, as store_distribution stores a calibration's: an MCMC's chain after burn-in, or UQ_options.num_samples (default 2000) draws of the Gaussian, those outside the params_for_id bounds dropped (step_result.json counts them). A later calibration takes it with priors_from. The run itself is in <step_id>/uq/. run_uq(inp_data_dict, best_param_vals, method) in libcuflynx.scripts.param_id_run_script runs the same outside a workflow, and do_uq with UQ_options.method: laplace runs the Laplace approximation after a calibration. An empty UQ_options ({}, what the builder's add_uq() writes when given no uq_options) is MCMC with the defaults below, or the workflow's UQ_options when it has some.

UQ_options key Default Used by method mcmc (or laplace) every uq step library emcee (also zeus, pymc) mcmc num_steps 5000 mcmc num_walkers 2 × the number of parameters mcmc burn_in 0.5 (below 1 a fraction of num_steps, else a number of steps) mcmc, and the posterior predictive check's draws from its chain num_samples 2000 draws of the Gaussian, before those outside the bounds are dropped laplace posterior_predictive true every uq step posterior_predictive_samples 100 the posterior predictive check

A uq step then runs the posterior predictive check (libcuflynx.param_id.posterior_predictive): the model at UQ_options.posterior_predictive_samples (default 100) posterior draws, from the MCMC chain after burn_in or from the Laplace approximation's stored samples, and how often the data lies inside the model's intervals. It is written to <step_id>/posterior_predictive/ (posterior_predictive.npz with the draws and predictions, posterior_predictive_coverage.json, and posterior_predictive_series.npz with the traces of the first draws), and step_result.json names them (posterior_predictive_dir, posterior_predictive_draws, posterior_predictive_coverage, posterior_predictive_series) with a summary under posterior_predictive_summary (num_samples, samples_that_failed_to_simulate, drawn_from: chain or samples, and each level's predictive_coverage and sample_interval_coverage). UQ_options.posterior_predictive: false skips it. A check that fails is a warning, with its message in posterior_predictive_summary.error: the step's distribution stands.

{"id": "posterior", "kind": "uq", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...", "params_for_id": "...",
 "result_from": "fit", "settings": {"UQ_options": {"method": "laplace", "num_samples": 2000},
                                    "ia_options": {"gradient_source": "FSA"}}}

After its fit, a calibration step writes what cuflynx-plot writes for a calibration: the observables at the best fit, with the error vectors percent_error_vec.npy and error_vec_names.npy (CA#341), in its run directory; and, when its model is a CellML, <step_id>/<step_id>_calibrated.cellml, the step's model with the best fit written in. step_result.json names them (percent_error_vec, error_vec_names, calibrated_model); a failure to write them is a warning, and the fit stands. When the obs_data has held-out data (prediction items with a value), the step also checks the best fit against it, as cuflynx-plot does: it writes validation_results.json in its run directory (validation_results in the result) and records each item's statistics under validation (data_item_name, n_points, rmse, nrmse, mean_abs_z, within_2std, ...; the series are in the file). A params_for_id modifier entry is calibrated as its theta (best_fit), and the parameters it modifies take modifier(theta, baseline): those values are what calibrated, the merged target and the calibrated CellML hold, and modifiers in the result records each entry's theta, targets, baselines and values. A local sensitivity step records the point it linearised about under nominal (source: its result_from step or model; the parameters and their values) and its signed coefficients under local_sensitivity_signed (see Local sensitivity files), and an identifiability or uq step its point under at and at_source. An identifiability step runs the method its ia_options.method names: Laplace, recorded under laplace, or profile_likelihood (with num_points, range_factor and optimiser_options), which profiles each parameter about that point. Its files are in profile_likelihood/ in the step's param_id/ directory (profile_likelihood_dir), and profile_likelihood in the result lists each parameter's file, the value profiled about (best_val), its cost and its 95% interval (ci_95).

{"id": "profiles", "kind": "identifiability", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...",
 "params_for_id": "...", "result_from": "fit",
 "settings": {"ia_options": {"method": "profile_likelihood", "num_points": 21,
                             "range_factor": 0.2}}}

Every calibrated CellML (a step's, the target's <stem>_calibrated.cellml, a CellML step's generated model, and a calibration's <prefix>_calibrated.cellml) is written by one writer, libcuflynx.param_id.calibrated_model: a model with imports, as a generated one has, is flattened into one file; a single-file model keeps its form, with only the values changed. See The calibrated model.

A set step declares values nothing fitted, so they are visible to everything downstream. Each entry names a parameter as the target does, and gives a reason:

{"id": "sglt1_amount", "kind": "set", "set": [
  {"parameter": "SGLT1/Scale_SGLT1", "scale": 14, "of": "sglt1_fit",
   "reason": "the amount the whole-cell flux needs"},
  {"parameter": "GLUT2_api/Scale_GLUT2", "value": 10, "reason": "kept from the source model"},
  {"parameter": "Kir/g_K", "scale": 3.37, "of": "inherited", "reason": "raised at this condition"}
]}

value sets a number. scale multiplies the value named by of: a calibration or set step (which runs first), or inherited, the value the target itself gives the parameter. A later step takes the values with fixed_from, and they are merged into the target with the calibrated values, in run order, so a later step's value wins a parameter both give. They are marked set_by_hand, with their reason, in the provenance diagram, the target's parameters and the calibrated parameters file, and are never reported as calibrated.

A set step with "point": true declares a point only: a place to start a fit (start_from) or to analyse at (result_from, or fixed_from). Its values are not merged into the target, so it gives the target no value of a parameter it shares with a calibration. The provenance diagram marks it set by hand, labelled "point only, not in the target". CUFLynx writes its slider positions, nominal points and best-fit points this way. The key is explicit, rather than inferred from how other steps use the step, so a workflow's meaning does not change when a step is added. The builder's add_set(..., point=True).

{"id": "sliders-1", "kind": "set", "point": true, "set": [
  {"parameter": "Lotka_Volterra_module/alpha", "value": 4.2, "reason": "slider position"}]}

A params_for_id modifier entry is calibrated as its theta, which acts on the parameters it modifies (scale: theta times each one's value in the model). Its point is therefore a theta, not a value of those parameters, and a point set step gives it with an entry and a theta (the builder's set_theta(entry, theta, reason=)), naming the modifier entry in the params_for_id of the steps that take it:

{"id": "sliders-2", "kind": "set", "point": true, "set": [
  {"entry": "alpha_scale", "theta": 0.9, "reason": "slider position"},
  {"parameter": "Lotka_Volterra_module/gamma", "value": 2.8, "reason": "slider position"}]}

A step with start_from or result_from that step starts or is analysed at theta 0.9, and alpha keeps its value in the step's model, so theta, its min and max and its prior mean what the params_for_id says. A calibration gives the thetas it fitted the same way: a step with result_from (or start_from) a calibration that has the same modifier entry is at its fitted theta, about the model's values, rather than at theta 1 about the fitted parameters. The step runs with a copy of its params_for_id that has theta on those entries (<step_id>/<step_id>_params_for_id.json). A theta entry is refused in a set step without "point": true (a theta is not a value of the target) and in a step whose params_for_id has no modifier entry of that name. With no theta given, an analysis of a modifier entry is at the theta that leaves its parameters at the model's values.

A sweep runs its model at each point and keeps every run. It feeds nothing forward: no step can take from it, and its values do not reach the target. It can start from values with fixed_from or at a calibration's result with result_from:

{"id": "sglt1_dose", "kind": "sweep", "model": "resources/enterocyte_module_array.json",
 "result_from": "whole_cell", "settings": {"sim_time": 100.0},
 "sweep": {"design": "grid", "outputs": ["enterocyte/c_Na"],
           "parameters": {"SGLT1/Scale_SGLT1": {"min": 1, "max": 20, "points": 7, "scale": "log"},
                          "Kir/A_Kir": {"values": [0, 1, 2]}}}}

A parameter is named as in a params_for_id and takes [min, max], {"min", "max", "points", "scale"} (5 points by default; "scale": "log" spaces them by ratio), {"values": [...]}, or {"factors": [...]}, multiples of the value the step's model gives it, or both: {"values": [1, 10, 100], "factors": [1]} is 1, 10, 100 and the model's value. design is grid, every combination, or one_at_a_time, each parameter's values with the others at the model's values. outputs are variables recorded over time. An obs_data gives the protocol in place of sim_time and pre_time, and its prediction_items with an operation give one feature per point. Each feature is drawn against the swept parameters as a feature_vs_input plot, for one_at_a_time or a grid of at most two parameters. A sweep does not read data_items.

A prediction run on the calibrated model takes "on_target": true in place of model and fixed_from. It runs on the target, given every calibration's and set step's values as the target merges them (a later step wins), after all of them. In the diagram it sits below the merged box, with one box under it naming the files it wrote: their folder once, then each file, done only when every file exists. Parameters that move together go in a zip group: the i-th point takes each member's i-th value, so their lists have one length, and the design treats the group as one parameter. With "parameters": {} the sweep is one run of its protocol. A long rest before a run, or the same run at several levels of an input, is the obs_data protocol: every point runs all its experiments and sub-experiments.

{"id": "energy_cost", "kind": "sweep", "on_target": true,
 "obs_data": "protocols/rest_then_glucose_15_40_obs_data.json", "settings": {"dt": 1.0},
 "sweep": {"outputs": ["enterocyte/v_NKA"], "zip": [["GLUT2_api/Scale_GLUT2", "GLUT2_bas/Scale_GLUT2"]],
           "parameters": {"GLUT2_api/Scale_GLUT2": {"values": [0, 0.1, 1, 10]},
                          "GLUT2_bas/Scale_GLUT2": {"values": [1, 1, 10, 100]}}}}

docs.title: Protocol factors
docs.text:
A step's protocol can give a parameter as factors on the value the step's model gives it, rather than as values: protocol_info.params_to_change_factors, in the shape of params_to_change. The workflow resolves them once per step (calibration, analysis or sweep), against the step model's values after fixed_from / result_from (on the target, the merged values), into params_to_change in a copy of the obs_data the step reads, <step_id>/inputs/<step_id>_obs_data.json. So x1 to x10 of the Kir density another step calibrated need no copy of its value:

"protocol_info": {"pre_times": [0, 0, 0], "sim_times": [[60], [60], [60]],
                  "params_to_change_factors": {"Kir/Scale_Kir": [[1], [2], [10]]}}

The step's step_result.json lists each value the factors multiplied under protocol_factors (parameter, base, units and, for a value an earlier step gave, from_step), and the diagram names them in the step's box. A parameter is refused in both params_to_change and params_to_change_factors, or when the step calibrates or sweeps it. Outside a workflow there is no step model to take values from, so parse_obs_data_json refuses the key.

The runs are in <step_id>/sweep/: sweep_results.npz has points, failed, parameters, outputs, features and feature_values, and for each experiment time_<e> and trace_<e> (points, outputs, times); sweep_manifest.json has the design, each parameter's values and the errors. Under MPI the points are spread across the ranks. A failed point stays as a NaN row, and the step fails only when every point fails.

A simulate step is one run of a model through its protocol: the simulation behind a figure, with the values a calibration found (result_from), values fixed by earlier steps (fixed_from) or the merged target ("on_target": true). It is a sweep of no parameters and writes the same files, so whatever reads a sweep reads it. simulate.outputs names the variables recorded over time; with an obs_data its protocol is run and its prediction_items give features. The prediction items that carry a value (held-out data) are compared with the model in <step_id>/sweep/validation_results.json, as cuflynx-run-predictions compares them; a sweep of more than one point writes no validation.

{"id": "paper_run", "kind": "simulate", "on_target": true,
 "obs_data": "protocols/glucose_step_obs_data.json", "settings": {"dt": 1.0},
 "simulate": {"outputs": ["enterocyte/c_Na", "enterocyte/v_NKA"]}}

A figure step calls a Python function that draws from the results of other steps; see Figure steps.

A reduction chooses the parameters a calibration fits from a Sobol sensitivity step, and writes those entries of the sensitivity step's params_for_id -- bounds and all -- as <step_id>/<step_id>_params_for_id.json, with its report param_reduction.json beside it. Its options are settings.param_reduction_options, as in user_inputs.yaml (see Parameter reduction) without the paths: method: pca (default) keeps one parameter per PCA mode of the outputs that moves the data by more than its noise; method: sobol keeps the n_params with the highest index. "param_reduction_options": {} is pca with every default. The options belong to the reduction step alone: the workflow's own settings (and any other step's) refuse them. min_mode_std is measured over the Sobol samples, which fill the whole prior box of the sensitivity step's params_for_id: it is a global, prior-wide measure, not local to the fitted values.

{"id": "screen", "kind": "sensitivity", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...",
 "params_for_id": "candidates_params_for_id.json",
 "settings": {"sa_options": {"method": "sobol", "num_samples": 256}}},
{"id": "keep", "kind": "reduction", "sensitivity_from": "screen",
 "settings": {"param_reduction_options": {"method": "pca"}}},
{"id": "fit", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...", "params_for_id_from": "keep"},
{"id": "ia", "kind": "identifiability", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...",
 "params_for_id": "fitted_params_for_id.json", "result_from": "fit",
 "settings": {"ia_options": {"method": "Laplace", "gradient_source": "FD"}}}

Rerunning screen reruns keep, and so fit and ia, since each takes from the one before.

A reduction may instead record a choice made by hand: "method": "manual" keeps the parameters named, for the reason given. It reads no sensitivity step (it has no sensitivity_from) and names the params_for_id whose entries, with their bounds, it keeps. A parameter is named as its params_for_id entry is labelled: vessel/variable, a grouped entry's names joined by +, or a modifier's name.

{"id": "keep", "kind": "reduction", "params_for_id": "candidates_params_for_id.json",
 "settings": {"param_reduction_options": {
     "method": "manual", "parameters": ["heart/E_lv_A", "aortic_root/C"],
     "reason": "the two the pressure data resolve; the rest are from the literature"}}},
{"id": "fit", "model": {...}, "obs_data": "...", "params_for_id_from": "keep"}

The names are checked against the params_for_id, and the step that fits them against its model, before anything runs. The provenance graph marks the step's box set_by_hand, with the names and the reason: no value is set by hand, but what is calibrated is. Editing the params_for_id or the choice reruns keep and what takes from it. The builder's add_reduction(id, method='manual', parameters=, reason=, params_for_id=).

A reduction is a libcuflynx.sensitivity_analysis.parameter_reduction.ParamReduction, which can also be used on its own:

from libcuflynx.sensitivity_analysis.parameter_reduction import ParamReduction
ParamReduction.from_options({'method': 'pca'}).reduce(
    'sa_results/', 'candidates_params_for_id.json', 'reduction/kept_params_for_id.json')

An emulator can be trained on the kept parameters alone, and MCMC run on it: an emulation step with "params_for_id_from": "keep", then a calibration with the same params_for_id_from, "emulator_from" that step and "store_distribution": true.

docs.title: How values move between models
docs.text:
A value is named by its module and parameter (aortic_root/C, which is C_aortic_root in the generated model), and moves through the target's names:

  • A module array keeps its module names. A value calibrated on aortic_root in one model fixes aortic_root in another, and lands on aortic_root in the target. When the names differ, module_map renames the step's modules into the target's.
  • A library module is generated alone as one module named mod, so its params_for_id targets are mod/<param> (mod/<submodule>/<param> for a supermodule) and its obs_data operands mod/<variable>. In the target it is renamed to where it sits: the submodule i_M of a supermodule target (rho_M_mod__i_M in the model, i_M/rho_M in its parameterisation), or the module of a module-array target that it is.

Each value a step calibrates or sets is recorded in its step_result.json with its module, param and model_name.

--dry-run checks that every calibrated parameter lands on a module the target has, and prints where each one lands and what each step is given. After the run, a value with no parameter of its name in the target is an error. A value passed to a model that lacks its module (an aorta value into a model without that module) is left out of that model with a warning.

A workflow file whose steps name vessel or vessel_map, or a run whose step_result.json records name vessel, is refused. Convert it once with cuflynx-upgrade workflow <workflow file or directory>: given a directory (a study, or a workflow's output directory), it converts every workflow file and step_result.json below it.

The other checks: a step's files exist; a library module exists in the library, and is in the target; a target written as a library module names its parameter set with parameterisation (instance is an error). The schema is libcuflynx/schemas/calibration_workflow.schema.json.

docs.title: One value per parameter
docs.text:
The target, and every step, is given one value of a parameter. When two steps give the same parameter:

  • One takes from the other, directly or through other steps (fixed_from, start_from, priors_from, ...): the later one's value replaces the earlier one's, with no warning. A step calibrates a parameter itself even when fixed_from would give it a value. So nka, then whole_cell with "fixed_from": ["nka"], may both fit the same scale: whole_cell's is used. To update an earlier calibration with new data rather than replace it, take the parameter out of the later step's params_for_id and list the earlier step in its priors_from (below), so the earlier posterior becomes the prior.
  • One is a set step: a value set by hand replaces a calibrated one with no warning, and the provenance marks it set by hand. Between a set step and a step it does not take from, the later in run order is used. Two set steps that do not take from each other (one does not scale the other's value) setting one parameter give a warning, which names the one used.
  • Neither takes from the other (two calibrations, or combine steps): an error, which names the parameter, the steps and what they give it to (the target, or a step through its fixed_from or result_from). Add a combine step, which is its own box in the diagram:
{"id": "best", "kind": "combine", "combine_from": ["from_low", "from_high"],
 "combine": {"method": "best_fit"}}

A combine step gives one value for every parameter its inputs give. Later steps take from it (fixed_from, start_from, result_from, a set step's scale), and the target takes its values in place of its inputs'. It runs no model. Its step_result.json lists the values under calibrated, each with combined_from (the inputs that gave it).

  • best_fit takes every value from the calibration with the lowest cost (chosen_from; costs has each input's). Costs are comparable only between calibrations of the same obs_data with the same cost_type, so anything else is refused; the inputs calibrate the same parameters. Use it for fits of one problem from several starting points.
  • mean gives each parameter the mean over the inputs that give it. The inputs may be set steps, and need not give the same parameters.

For the target, the error comes where the target is merged for use: a run of more than one step, a sweep on_target, and writing the calibrated parameters. Reading the file, --dry-run (the plan's target_overlap holds the message) and a run of one step (--only) warn instead and use the later step's value, so a second calibration can be run before the combine step that settles it is added. A step given two values is always an error.

A step fitting a reduction's choice (params_for_id_from) is checked once the reduction has run, against what it kept, not against every candidate: the error then comes at the merge, with every step's result kept, so a run with --stale-only after adding the combine step runs only that step. A choice made by hand ("method": "manual") is known from the file, so a step fitting it is checked before anything runs, like any other calibration. The builder's add_combine(id, combine_from, method=).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
<output_dir>/                         --output-dir; default workflow_output/<workflow_name> beside the workflow file
    calibration_workflow.json         the workflow as run
    workflow_result.json              order, provenance (input hashes, times, commits, libCellML version), merged parameters
    provenance_graph.json             how every value was set, for reports and CUFLynx (below)
    provenance.svg                    that graph as a diagram to place in a report
    <step_id>/step_result.json        its kind; calibrated values, the fixed values and priors it was given, input hashes; an analysis's outputs and the point it analysed (at or nominal; not in fixed)
    <step_id>/model/                  the generated step model
    <step_id>/param_id/               the usual param_id outputs
    <step_id>/distribution/           with store_distribution
    <step_id>/sensitivity/            a sensitivity step's indices and plots
    <step_id>/emulator/               an emulation step's emulator
    <step_id>/<step_id>_laplace_*.npy an identifiability step's Laplace mean and covariance (also in step_result.json)
    <step_id>/<step_id>_calibrated.cellml  a calibration's model with its best fit (a CellML model)
    <step_id>/uq/                     a uq step's run: its MCMC run directory, or its Laplace mean and covariance
    <step_id>/posterior_predictive/   a uq step's posterior predictive check
    <step_id>/<step_id>_params_for_id.json a reduction's params_for_id
    _target/model/                    the target generated with every calibrated value
    models/<view>/                    a model generated for viewing (WorkflowBuilder.model); no step is named models
    <workflow_name>_cuflynx_study.json  the study manifest CUFLynx opens (below)
    inputs/workflows/<workflow_name>/<yyyy-mm-dd_HHMMSS>/   the workflow packed (--pack layout): every input it was run from

The manifest records the workflow as run, its result, the target and every step (its kind, model, obs_data, params_for_id, the steps it took something from, its status, run directory and outputs). It is updated as each step finishes, so CUFLynx can follow a running workflow. Each step's own manifest, in <step_id>/param_id/, links back to it. "write_cuflynx_study": false in the settings turns both off.

The output directory is the workflow's working dir (see The study working dir): the run packs the workflow into inputs/workflows/<workflow_name>/<yyyy-mm-dd_HHMMSS>/ (a new dated folder only when the packed workflow differs from one stored already) and the manifests name the packed copies, by paths relative to each manifest's folder, so the output directory can be zipped and opened anywhere. A step's manifest names the same copies (../../inputs/...). The one path left absolute is the --write-calibrated file, which is written beside the target. "cuflynx_study_copy_inputs": false in the settings packs nothing and names the inputs where they are.

--pack DIR (or pack_workflow in Python) copies every file the workflow needs to run, and none of its results, into the new directory DIR: DIR/calibration_workflow.json runs anywhere and gives the same results. --pack DIR --overwrite (pack_workflow(..., overwrite=True)) replaces an earlier pack in DIR; a directory holding anything a pack does not write is refused. It holds each step's files under inputs/<step_id>/, the module versions the workflow uses under modules/ (built-in modules come with libcuflynx), and the files its settings name under settings/. Paths in settings (external_modules_dir, *_funcs_external_path) are relative to the workflow file, like its other paths.

--from-step X reruns X and everything after it, reusing the earlier results (and refusing if their obs_data, params_for_id or parameters changed since); --only X reruns one step. --write-calibrated writes the merged set beside the target's parameters file, as <name>_calibrated_parameters.json (<name> is the module array's prefix or the parameterisation), in the target's nested form: the target's parameters file, completed with every other value the target's model uses (as its generated <prefix>_parameters.json holds them, each one's data_reference starting from <parameterisation>:), with each calibrated value set at its path (<vessel>/<variable> in a module array's file, the module's own path in a parameterisation's). So the result reproduces the run without the module library. The target's files are not changed. Each step's generated model, and the target's (_target/), has its own generated <prefix>_parameters.json: the values that model ran with. workflow_result.json names the target's as target_model.parameters_path.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
A run writes provenance_graph.json and provenance.svg when it finishes. The diagram opens a report: paste the SVG into the page, where it takes the page's text colour. cuflynx-provenance <output_dir> writes both again, and it needs only the output directory, not the module library. The graph's schema is libcuflynx/schemas/provenance_graph.schema.json. It is closed, so its schema_version goes up whenever it gains or changes a node kind, edge style or key, and a reader (read_provenance_graph, provenance_svg) refuses a version it does not know.

One box stands for each step, in order, with the model source, the measured values, the derived values, the values set by hand, the values calibrated before the run, and the target. Each value the target uses is marked with what set it:

Mark What set it Where it comes from calibrated a step fitted it the step's results calibrated an earlier calibration "origin": "calibrated", which a calibrated parameters file writes; its data_reference names the workflow and step measured a cited source "origin": "measured", with the source in data_reference derived a parameter derivation, from data "origin": "derived" and "derivation" naming it (tutorial/docs/parameter-derivations.md) inherited the original model; nothing constrains it "origin": "inherited" set by hand us, with a reason "origin": "set_by_hand" and a required "reason" unclassified nothing says no origin

A "Model source" box stands for the target's model, with an arrow to every step generated from it; a step whose model is another module array or library module has a source box of its own. A step's box names, by vessel/param and value, its priors (which step's posterior, and the fitted kind), the values it calibrated (its parameter count includes those priors_from adds) and the values earlier steps fixed, each with what set it: calibrated by which step on which obs_data, or set by hand in which step and why. The target's box names its merged values the same way. A box shows the first four of each list (six for the target and the model source) and says how many more the graph file has.

The boxes of values given in the parameters files (measured, derived, set by hand, calibrated before the run) point to the target's model source: those values are in the model of every step generated from it, so each calibration ran with them. When no step comes from that model source, they point to the target.

When a derived value's derivation has fixed_constants, a "Fixed constants of derivations" box with an arrow to the derived values lists each as <derivation>/<constant> with its value, units and origin (measured with its source, set by hand with its reason, inherited, or unclassified when the derivation declares none); it shows the first six and the graph file has them all. The diagram's footer counts the unclassified constants (1 unclassified constant) after the unclassified values, whenever there are fixed constants, so none hides behind a zero.

A value is never counted as inherited by default, so an unclassified count above zero says which values still need describing. workflow_result.json records the libcuflynx commit, the commit of the repository holding the workflow file, whether tracked files had changed in each, and the libCellML version. A commit is null outside a repository.

Each step's inputs show as current, stale or missing. A step's result is stale when its files or settings changed since it ran, or when a step it took something from is stale or ran again after it, and a later step refuses to reuse it (Run the workflow from ...). A changed module library is shown and warned about but does not make a step stale, because a library holds far more than one model uses. A build before the workflow is not tracked.

A figure step is a box like any other step, with a dotted arrow from each step it reads, labelled with what it reads, and one box under it naming the files it wrote. Its inputs in the graph are its declaration (settings), its script and each file it lists, each current, stale or missing.

docs.title: Figure steps
docs.text:
A figure of a workflow is a step: a Python function in a script file, given the results of the steps it names. libcuflynx loads the results and calls the function, so the figure is drawn by the run, is out of date when anything it reads changes, and is in the provenance diagram and the packed workflow.

{"id": "dose_response", "kind": "figure",
 "function": "figures/dose_response.py:draw",
 "inputs": {"curves": {"sweep": "sglt1_dose"},
            "fit": {"values": "whole_cell"},
            "data": {"obs_data": "whole_cell"}},
 "files": ["figures/paper_style.py"]}

function is <script>.py:<function>, the script's path relative to the workflow file. Each entry of inputs is one parameter of the function, by name, and what it is given: {"<kind>": "<step>"}. The function's parameters are exactly those names and out_dir; this is checked when the workflow is read, without running the script. files lists other files the script reads or imports (helpers, a style module beside it).

Input kind Read from a The function gets sweep sweep or simulate step the arrays of sweep_results.npz as a dict: points, failed, parameters, outputs, features, feature_values, and time_<e>, trace_<e> (points, outputs, times) per experiment; and manifest, sweep_manifest.json as its JSON document validation simulate step (a sweep of one point) validation_results.json as its JSON document: items, per prediction item that carries a value its data_item_name, operation, unit, data_type, n_points, rmse, nrmse, mean_abs_z, within_2std, and t, data, std, model at the observation times values calibration, set or combine step {"<module>/<parameter>": value}: what it calibrated, set by hand or combined, named as a params_for_id names them (a nested module by its path, heart/lv/E; a global as global/R; a combine step: as the target names them) obs_data step with an obs_data the obs_data file as its JSON document params_for_id step with a params_for_id, or a reduction the params_for_id it ran with (a reduction: the one it wrote) as its JSON document sensitivity sensitivity step Sobol indices, {"S1": {output: {parameter: value}}, "ST": {...}} (empty for a local analysis); and local, {"relative": {output: {parameter: value}}, "absolute": {...}} from a local analysis (sa_options.method: "local"), else None progress calibration step the optimiser's history (param_id.run_history.read_run_history): param_labels, cost_history (per generation, best first), param_history_norm (0-1), grad_history, starts (per multi-start: cost, params in actual values), best_cost; and param_mins, param_maxs, the params_for_id bounds fit_errors calibration step the best fit's error per data_item, which a calibration writes when it ends: names, percent_error (100 (model - data) / data), std_error ((model - data) / std; a series: averaged over its points) and data_references, in obs_data order best_fit calibration step the best fit against its data, from the outputs a calibration saves per experiment it fits (all_outputs_with_best_param_vals_exp_<e>.npz) and its obs_data: items, per data_item its data_item_name, trace_name, data_type, operation, operation_kwargs, plot_type (a constant without one: horizontal), unit, experiment_idx, subexperiment_idx, window (its subexperiment's start and end), value, std, data_reference, t and model (its first operand over its subexperiment; None when the solver did not log it, as Myokit does not log a constant), obs_t (a series: the times of its values) and fit (a constant: the calibrated model's value, from the best fit's std error); and experiment_labels mcmc_chain calibration with store_distribution its MCMC chain: chain, an array (steps, walkers, parameters) cut to the draws every walker reached; param_labels; burn_in_index, the first step after the burn-in its UQ options give emulator_validation emulation step the held-out points of emulator_validation.npz in real units: theta (points, parameters), y_true and y_pred (points, features), feature_labels, param_entry_labels; and feature_r2, feature_rmse, feature_nrmse from emulator_metadata.json (None where not recorded) distribution calibration with store_distribution, or uq step {"names": [...], "samples": array (samples, parameters)}, named by the model's names laplace identifiability step, or uq step with method laplace {"parameters": [...], "mean", "covariance", "std"} as arrays posterior_predictive uq step (with posterior_predictive, the default) its posterior predictive check: labels (one per scalar observable), predictions (draws, observables), ground_truth, std and thetas as arrays; coverage, posterior_predictive_coverage.json as its JSON document; and series, when it kept traces, {"meta": {time, observables, segments, experiment_labels}, "traces": {"<segment>|<variable>": array (draws, points)}, "time": {"<segment>": array}}, else None profile_likelihood identifiability step with method profile_likelihood {"nll_threshold_95", "profiles": [{"parameter", "param_values", "costs", "best_val", "best_cost", "ci_95"}]}, the sweeps as arrays reduction reduction step its report (param_reduction.json: reduction, selected, ...); for a PCA reduction also modes, [{mode, variance, variance_share, informative, loadings: {feature: value}}], and mode_indices, {"S1": {"mode_<k>": {parameter: value}}, "ST": {...}} (both None for a Sobol reduction)

The function writes its files into out_dir and returns their paths:

"""Na against the SGLT1 scale, with the fitted value marked."""
import os

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def draw(curves, fit, data, out_dir):
    scale = curves['points'][:, 0]
    sodium = curves['trace_0'][:, 0, -1]
    with plt.style.context('seaborn-v0_8-paper'):
        figure, axes = plt.subplots()
        axes.semilogx(scale, sodium)
        axes.axvline(fit['SGLT1/Scale_SGLT1'], linestyle=':')
        path = os.path.join(out_dir, 'dose_response.png')
        figure.savefig(path, dpi=200)
        plt.close(figure)
    return [path]


def main(argv=None):
    from libcuflynx.calibration_workflow.figures import figure_main
    return figure_main(draw, argv)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Rules a figure function follows:

  • It runs no simulation. Every simulation is a step with its own protocol (a sweep, or a simulate step for one run), so each run is recorded and the figure only reads results. A figure that needs a curve at the calibrated values reads a simulate step with "on_target": true or result_from.
  • It sets its style inside the function. The function is called with Matplotlib's settings as the rc file gives them, whatever was drawn or imported before, so the figure does not depend on what ran before it. Settings changed at the top of the script do not reach the call.
  • It has a main, as above, so the script also runs on its own on a finished run, through the same loaders and so with the same objects:
python figures/dose_response.py <run directory> [--step dose_response] [--out-dir DIR]
python figures/dose_response.py <run directory> --input curves=sweep:sglt1_dose \
    --input fit=values:whole_cell --input data=obs_data:whole_cell

The first form draws the run's figure step that names this script (--step picks one of several); the second gives the inputs directly. Both give the files the workflow gives: the same file names, images equal pixel by pixel and other files byte for byte (libcuflynx.calibration_workflow.figures.output_differences(dir_a, dir_b) lists any difference, for a test of your own scripts). figure_main takes one function or a list of the script's figure functions.

The files are in <step_id>/figure/, listed under figures in the step's step_result.json. A figure step is out of date when its script, a file in files or its declaration changed, or a step it reads ran again after it. Every run draws the figure steps that are out of date and whose inputs are current, after its other steps, whatever --from-step or --only say; --only <figure step> draws that one regardless. A figure whose inputs are out of date waits. A figure that fails does not stop the other figures or the merge: its error is raised once the run's results are written. Figure steps pass nothing on, so the calibrated parameters file does not wait for them, and adding or changing a figure step after a run leaves the other steps current. pack_workflow copies each script with its files into figures/<step_id>/.

docs.title: Standard figures
docs.text:
libcuflynx ships a script of standard figures, one function per figure. Copy it beside the workflow and name its functions in figure steps; the copy is the workflow's own script, hashed and packed like any other, so a later libcuflynx does not change a finished run's figures:

from libcuflynx.calibration_workflow.figures import write_standard_figures
write_standard_figures('figures')   # figures/standard_figures.py; an existing copy is kept

{"id": "z_traces", "kind": "figure",
 "function": "figures/standard_figures.py:sweep_traces",
 "inputs": {"sweep": {"sweep": "scan"}}}

The input names are the function's parameters:

Function Draws Inputs sweep_traces per experiment, every output over time, a line per point (traces_exp_<e>.png) sweep: sweep sweep_features each feature against the swept parameters, as the sweep step draws them sweep: sweep prediction_plots the obs_data's prediction_plots, from a simulate step run on that obs_data; a time-course plot's output must be among the step's outputs simulation: sweep, obs_data: obs_data validation the held-out prediction items against the model: validation_scores.csv (per item n_points, rmse, nrmse, mean_abs_z, within_2std), the scalar items' data ± std against the model with y = x (validation_parity.png), and per series item the data ± std and the model from the start of its sub-experiment (validation_<item>.png) validation: validation protocol_inputs per experiment each params_to_change entry over the logged time: a number held over its sub-experiment, a trace or shape from the sub-experiment's start (inputs_exp_<e>.png) obs_data: obs_data sobol_indices S1 and ST per output (sobol_<output>.png) and an ST heatmap sensitivity: sensitivity local_sensitivity a heatmap of a local analysis's relative sensitivities, parameters by outputs (local_sensitivity_heatmap.png) sensitivity: sensitivity pca_modes per PCA mode its loading on each feature and the ST of each parameter (pca_mode_<k>.png), and ST per mode (pca_mode_ST_heatmap.png) reduction: reduction calibration_progress the best cost per generation on a log axis, with the band up to the worst recorded best cost (a genetic algorithm's top 10), or a line per start (cost_history.png); each parameter normalised by its bounds per generation (param_history.png) progress: progress best_fit per trace a data_item is measured on and experiment, as the calibration draws it (best_fit_<trace>_exp_<e>.png): the model's trace over the subexperiments its items read; a constant as a dashed line at its data over a ±1 std band and a solid line at the model's value (horizontal; horizontal_from_min from the trace's minimum; vertical a time); a series as its values with ±1 std bars. Units in m3, m3_per_s and J_per_m3 are drawn in cm^3, cm^3/s and kPa fit: best_fit mcmc_diagnostics per parameter each walker's trace (mcmc_chain.png), its running mean from step 0 and from the burn-in (mcmc_cumulative_mean.png), and its autocorrelation against lag with guides at ±0.1, titled "within" or "still correlated" over the last 20% of lags (mcmc_autocorrelation.png); at most 12 walkers and 400 steps drawn chain: mcmc_chain emulator_validation per feature the emulator against the simulator at the held-out points, with y = x, R2 and NRMSE (emulator_parity.png); per feature the normalised residual against each parameter (emulator_residuals_<feature>.png) emulator: emulator_validation posterior per parameter a histogram, its mean and 5-95% band (posterior.png) distribution: distribution laplace per parameter the normal density over ±4 std (laplace.png) laplace: laplace

The calibration fit plot and the error bars per observable are not among them yet: a calibration step does not save its best-fit outputs or error vectors.

A workflow's older external_figures key (commands that libcuflynx recorded but never ran) is refused: write each as a figure step. A script may call other software itself if it must.

docs.title: Distributions and priors
docs.text:
With "store_distribution": true (and UQ_options in the settings) a step runs MCMC after its fit and stores distribution/: the raw chain.npy, the post-burn-in samples.npy, stats.json (means, standard deviations, quantiles, covariance) and a manifest. In Python:

from libcuflynx.calibration_workflow import StoredDistribution
d = StoredDistribution.load('wf_out/M-type-K-channel')
d.sample(1000, rng=0)               # draws, shape (1000, n_params)
d.logpdf(x)                         # log density at a parameter vector
d.marginal('rho_M_mod')             # one parameter's samples
d.mapped_into('i_M').names          # named as in the supermodule: ['rho_M_mod_i_M']

A later step lists it in priors_from, either by id or as {"step": "M-type-K-channel", "kind": "mvnormal", "inflate": 1.0, "parameters": [...]}. parameters picks some of the stored parameters, by their names in the earlier step's model (rho_M_mod; its step_result.json lists them as calibrated[].model_name); without it, all of them. Those parameters are then calibrated again in the later step, with the stored posterior as a prior over all of them jointly. kind is how the samples are represented, each on a scale on which the parameter's bounds are unbounded (logit for [min, max], log for a lower bound only), so the density respects the bounds and can follow a skewed posterior:

kind Representation When mvnormal (default) multivariate normal: means and full covariance keeps correlations; exact and cheap normal independent normals when correlations should be dropped kde Gaussian kernel density estimate non-Gaussian posteriors with few (≲5) parameters

inflate multiplies the variance, to temper an overconfident earlier posterior. A prior only shapes the log posterior, so a step with priors_from must either sample it (store_distribution) or optimise it (optimiser_options.objective_function: likelihood, the genetic algorithm). In the first case its reported values are the posterior medians, since the optimiser's best fit ignores the prior (step_result.json says which: point_estimate).

docs.title: Expected outcome
docs.text: You should have a calibrated model in generated_models/[file_prefix]_[obs_file_name]/ and plots in param_id_output/.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If you see params_for_id_path ... does not exist, confirm params_for_id_file or file_prefix and your resources_dir.
  • If you see obs_dt is required for series entries, add obs_dt to each series data item in obs_data.json.
  • If MPI errors occur, ensure OpenMPI/MPICH is installed and mpi4py is available in your environment (pip install "libcuflynx[mpi]").

docs.title: Reduced-order models (ROMs)
docs.text:
A reduced-order model is a surrogate that is itself a dynamic model: a smaller system of equations, built from runs of the full model, that is integrated in time and returns the outputs as traces. An emulator answers only for the scalar features it was trained on; a ROM answers for any output and protocol it was built to cover.

This release of libcuflynx does not build ROMs: build one with your own tools. CA then runs it as a model:

  • Wrap the ROM in a solver class and name it as an external Python model: model_type: external_python, with external_model_path naming the file. The class declares the ROM's parameters and outputs and steps it in time.
  • Calibration, sensitivity analysis and the other analyses then run on it as they do on any external model, with the same obs_data and params_for_id. Series data, prediction items and plots work, because the ROM returns traces.
  • In a calibration workflow the ROM is a step's model, {"external_model_path": "my_rom.py"} (the builder's external_model(path)). A step on the full model and a step on the ROM can then sit in one workflow.

A ROM needs no key of its own: use_emulator, emulator_from and emulator_dir name emulators only. An emulator can also be trained on a ROM, as on any model.

Check a ROM against the full model before relying on it: run both on the same obs_data and compare the features and traces over the parameter ranges the analysis will visit.

docs.title: ABI HPC Standard
docs.text:
Clone the circulatory_autogen repo into a directory of your choice, create a virtual environment and install the project into it (python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -e ., see Getting Started), then activate it in the shell (or job script) the run starts from, so the user_run_files/*.sh helpers find the commands:

source {project_dir}/venv/bin/activate

Note

Use a venv, not an OpenCOR pythonshell: CA does not run in OpenCOR's bundled Python (its dual-ABI mpi4py can mismatch the cluster's mpiexec and abort every rank with unsupported PMI version PMIx). For the CVODE_libopencor solver, make the venv with Python 3.12 or later and pip install -e ".[libopencor]".

To run in parallel you need to load MPI before installing mpi4py and before each run. Do the following from the {project_dir}/user_run_files dir:

. load_mpi.sh

Then you should be able to run as normal from the user_run_files dir (e.g. ./run_param_id.sh <NUM_CORES> or ./run_sensitivity_analysis.sh <NUM_CORES>).

docs.title: Scratch space: TMPDIR
docs.text:
libCUFLynx writes a flattened copy of each CellML model to the system temp directory before Myokit compiles it, and caches it there between runs. That directory is /tmp by default, which on a compute node is often small, node-local, purged mid-job, or not writable by you at all.

You do not need sudo or a code change — set TMPDIR before launching and everything follows it:

export TMPDIR="$SCRATCH/tmp"   # or any directory you can write to
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"

Put this in your job script, before the run_*.sh call, so every rank inherits it. Python's tempfile reads TMPDIR (then TEMP, then TMP), so this covers every temp path the engine uses, not only the CellML cache.

Two notes for multi-rank jobs:

  • Node-local scratch is the better choice where you have it. The cache is a pure function of the input model, so every rank flattens the same file to the same name; writes are atomic (staged then os.replaced), which makes sharing one directory safe but pointless work.
  • Do not point TMPDIR at a directory that is purged while the job runs. The cache is read on every helper construction, not just the first.

docs.title: ABI HPC Extra
docs.text:
Any extra Python libraries go into your own venv with pip install <packagename> — the process is the same as on a local machine, see Getting Started. Because the venv is yours, nothing has to be shared with or re-installed alongside another user's environment.

Warning

Before installing mpi4py into the venv, make sure you load mpi with

module load mpi/mpich-x86_64 && echo "succesfully loaded mpi/mpich-x86_64"

mpi4py compiles against whichever MPI is loaded at install time, so loading it afterwards is too late.

docs.title: Sensitivity Analysis
docs.text:
Sensitivity Analysis (SA) is a recommended first step in the calibration pipeline because it performs crucial parameter screening. Calibration is the process of tuning numerous model parameters (inputs) until the model's output matches experimental data. Without SA, a modeler might waste weeks tuning parameters that have virtually no impact on the final result, or unknowingly tune parameters that are highly correlated, leading to non-unique solutions. SA efficiently identifies:

  • Influential parameters: Which parameters contribute most significantly to the model's output variance.

  • Non-influential parameters: Which parameters can be fixed or ignored, drastically simplifying the calibration space.

SA ensures that the calibration effort is focused, efficient, and physically meaningful.

docs.title: The Sobol Method
docs.text:
The Sobol method is a powerful, global, variance-based sensitivity analysis technique. Unlike local methods that only test parameter changes one at a time, the Sobol method explores the entire input space simultaneously.

  • Key Feature: It quantifies the contribution of each individual input parameter (First-Order Index, S_i) and the contribution of parameter interactions (Second-Order, Total-Order Index, S_{Ti}) to the overall output variance.

This comprehensive approach allows modelers to understand not only which parameters are important on their own, but also how complex, synergistic interactions between two or more parameters drive the final simulation results.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A generated model and obs_data.json file (see Parameter Identification).
  • A params_for_id.json file defining parameter ranges.
  • pip install "libcuflynx[mpi]" (and a system MPI toolchain) if running in parallel.

docs.title: SA in Circulatory_Autogen
docs.text:
Since Sensitivity Analysis (SA) is intertwined with parameter identification, you will need the same input files as required for parameter identification. This includes both the params_for_id.json and the obs_data.json files. However, the exact values of the data terms in the observation file are not critical for SA itself, as you are simply exploring parameter space and variance, not matching the simulation output to observed data.

Crucially, each data item defined in your obs_data.json file is treated as a feature for SA, meaning you will receive a separate set of plots (one for first and total order indices, and one for second order indices) for each data item.

docs.title: Configuration for user_inputs.yaml
docs.text:
To run the Sobol analysis, you need to add a sa_options block to your user_inputs.yaml configuration file: 

sa_options: 
    method: 'sobol' 
    num_samples: 1024 
    sample_type: saltelli
    output_dir: <SA_outputs_path>
The available options for method are 'sobol' and 'local' (derivatives at one point; see Local sensitivity files). num_samples and sample_type are for sobol only. Available sample types are ['saltelli']. What we call num_samples here is actually the num_samples in

actual_num_samples = num_samples (2M+2)

where M is the number of parameters. This means the num_samples that you set doesn't need to be dependent on M.

An indicator that the sample size may be too low is the observation of relatively large negative values for the Sobol indices in the results; if this occurs, increase the sample size and re-run the analysis.

If sa_options is omitted, defaults are applied:

  • method: sobol
  • num_samples: 32
  • sample_type: saltelli
  • output_dir: <param_id_output_dir>/sensitivity, in the study's working dir (see The study working dir). A relative output_dir is taken under that folder and an absolute one is used as given. With cuflynx_study_copy_inputs: false (or write_cuflynx_study: false) the default is sensitivity_outputs/<file_prefix>_SA_results, and a relative output_dir is taken under sensitivity_outputs/.

docs.title: Prediction items as extra outputs
docs.text:
Set include_prediction_items: true in sa_options to also report the sensitivity of the prediction_items in obs_data.json that have an operation (see Prediction items as scalar features). They are not in the cost, so they are useful for asking which parameters drive a quantity you predict rather than fit.

sa_options:
    method: sobol
    num_samples: 1024
    include_prediction_items: true
  • Only scalar prediction items with an operation are included: data_type: constant, or no data and a reducing operation such as max. Items without an operation, and series, are skipped with a warning that names them. An operation that returns more than one number is an error.
  • They come after the data_item outputs. They are labelled by their data_item_name, as <data_item_name> (Exp<e>, Sub<s>), in the Sobol CSVs (all_outputs_n<N>_Sobol_indices.csv columns S1_.../ST_..., and all_outputs_n<N>_Sobol_2nd_order_indices.csv), the per-output plots and the heatmaps. The sub-experiment is the item's subexperiment_idx (by default its experiment's last), which is the one the operation is applied to. A feature measured in an experiment that has no data_items (a validation-only experiment) makes the SA simulate that experiment too. Without the option, such an experiment is not simulated.
  • The run also writes sobol_output_features.json, which lists every output column with its kind (data_item, prediction_item or cost), data_item_name, experiment_idx and subexperiment_idx.
  • With method: local they are extra rows of local_sensitivity_absolute.csv and local_sensitivity_relative.csv, named by data_item_name, and of local_sensitivity_signed.csv, named as their Sobol columns. get_local_sensitivities() lists them under prediction_feature_names. They are computed the same way as the data_item rows: by the analytic arm (CasADi, or Myokit CVODES sensitivities), or by central finite differences with fd_rel_step (2M more simulations) when gradient_method: FD or over an emulator. Myokit's arm needs every prediction feature in one and the same sub-experiment; otherwise (features in two experiments, or in an experiment with several sub-experiments) they fall back to finite differences, with a warning.
  • choose_most_impactful_params_sobol ranks over every column in the CSV, prediction features included.
  • With use_emulator: true the emulator must have been trained with emulator_settings.include_prediction_items: true. If it was not, the run stops and says to retrain.

Without the option, nothing changes: the outputs and files are exactly the data_item ones.

docs.title: Local sensitivity files (method: local)
docs.text:
method: local differentiates each scalar feature Y with respect to each parameter p at one point (the model's values, or a workflow step's result_from), and writes three CSVs to output_dir. Each has an output column and one column per parameter, named by its entry label (a grouped row joins its members with +; a modifier uses its own name):

File Value Rows labelled local_sensitivity_absolute.csv dY/dp as the engine labels an observable (<item_name_for_plotting>, with [exp e, sub s] only when that repeats) local_sensitivity_relative.csv |p| dY/dp / |Y|; 0.0 where Y = 0 as the absolute file local_sensitivity_signed.csv d ln Y / d ln p = (p / Y) dY/dp; NaN where Y = 0, where it is undefined as the Sobol outputs: <item_name_for_plotting> (Exp<e>, Sub<s>), made unique the same way

The signed file says which way a feature moves: -1 means a 1% rise in p lowers Y by about 1%. The relative file keeps the sign of dY/dp only, so the two disagree where p or Y is negative. Its row labels are the column names of all_outputs_n<N>_Sobol_indices.csv (after S1_ and ST_), so one heatmap can show a Sobol index and a local coefficient of one observable side by side. get_local_sensitivities() returns the matrices (absolute, relative, signed) with signed_output_names, nominal_param_vals and nominal_feature_vals. A workflow's local sensitivity step names the signed file in its step_result.json, as local_sensitivity_signed.

docs.title: How to run SA script
docs.text:
First, ensure you have the required sensitivity analysis packages specified in Getting Started.

To run the script, use the following command (which utilizes MPI for parallelized computation on CPU):

./run_sensitivity_analysis.sh <NUM_CORES>

After successful execution, you will find the SA plots—including the first, second, and total order indices—in the directory specified by output_dir.

docs.title: Parameter reduction
docs.text:
A Sobol analysis can choose the parameters to calibrate, for two reasons:

  1. Redundancy. Parameters that move the data the same way cannot be told apart. Keep one parameter per direction the data can fix. On the 3compartment study (benchmarks/param_reduction_3compartment) calibrating all seven parameters is not identifiable (the Fisher information is singular or has condition number about 1e16), while the reduced fits have condition numbers of 12-16 and agree between seeds.
  2. Noise-blindness. A large Sobol index on an output that moves by less than its noise is not worth fitting. The reduction measures every effect in units of the obs_data noise.
